title: [Mac Users] Installation and Setup for Web3 Development
section: 37. Web3 Decentralised App (DApp) Development with the Internet Computer
summary: Mac walkthrough for installing Node LTS, the dfx SDK, VS Code with the Motoko extension, then creating, starting, deploying and running a Hello World Internet Computer project locally.

concepts.heading: Prerequisites and tools
points: The lesson links a published document with every command; the installer command must be copied whole, because dropping the trailing quote breaks it.
Node.js: use the LTS release, not the newest feature release, because the Internet Computer tooling targets LTS. Check with node --version; the lecture asks for version 16 or above.

dfx: the DFINITY command-line SDK used to run a local Internet Computer, build and deploy canisters, and execute code. Installed by pasting a one-line install command into Terminal (open via Spotlight). Verify with dfx --version (0.9.3 in the video). (Extra) The current installer and version numbers differ now; always use the up-to-date command from the DFINITY docs.
VS Code plus the extension named Motoko published by the DFINITY Foundation (several similarly named extensions exist). It gives syntax support for the Motoko language.

concepts.heading: Project folder and scaffolding
points: Create a single parent folder (ic-projects) in the home directory to hold all Internet Computer projects.

In Terminal, cd into it (typing cd then dragging the folder in fills the path), then run the dfx new command with a project name. This generates a sample app: Motoko backend code, HTML/JavaScript frontend, and config. The DFINITY logo printed in the terminal signals completion.
Open the generated folder in VS Code via Open to browse the Motoko, HTML and JS files.

concepts.heading: Run and deploy locally
points: Terminal 1: dfx start launches the local replica (the local Internet Computer network). Wait for the server-listening info message and leave it running.
Terminal 2 (split terminal button in VS Code): dfx deploy builds the project and installs its canisters on the local network. It takes a while the first time.
Then npm start serves the frontend; the printed URL opens the app.
The sample page has a name input and button that calls the backend greet function and shows a greeting. Seeing it work proves the toolchain is set up.

code_examples.caption: Mac setup sequence (summary of lesson steps)
code_examples.code:
node --version          # want 16+ (use the LTS release)
# install dfx using the one-line installer command from the lesson's Google doc (copy it whole, including closing quotes)
dfx --version           # lecture shows 0.9.3
mkdir ~/ic-projects && cd ~/ic-projects
dfx new hello_world     # scaffolds the sample project (sample Motoko + frontend)
cd hello_world
# terminal 1
dfx start               # starts the local Internet Computer replica; wait for the 'listening' info line
# terminal 2
dfx deploy              # builds and installs canisters on the local network
npm start               # dev server; open the URL it prints

task.name: Install tools and run the Hello World canister app
task.starting_point: A Mac with Terminal; VS Code optional until step 4.
task.goal: Have a local Internet Computer replica running and the sample DApp greeting you in the browser.
steps: Check node --version is 16+ (install the LTS build if not).
Run the dfx installer command from the lesson document, then confirm with dfx --version.
Install VS Code and the Motoko extension from the DFINITY Foundation.
Create ic-projects in your home folder, cd into it, run dfx new with a project name.
Open the project folder in VS Code.
In one terminal run dfx start and wait for the listening message; in a second run dfx deploy, then npm start.
Open the printed URL, enter your name, press the button and confirm the greeting.
task.expected_result: The browser page shows a name box and a button; submitting returns a greeting with your name.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 37 - Web3 Decentralised App (DApp) Development with the Internet Computer/37.06 [Mac Users] Installation and Setup for Web3 Development/README.md (instructions only; PDF alongside)

pitfalls: Installing Node's current release instead of LTS.
Truncating the pasted installer command (missing closing quote).
Closing the dfx start terminal before deploying; it must keep running.
(Extra) Newer dfx versions scaffold a different layout (hello_backend / hello_frontend with Vite) and may use dfx start --background and different install commands; follow current docs.
